natural: one branch from the cassia grove

meaning.en: A modest way of saying one is outstanding; also, a person of rare talent among many.
meaning.zh: 原为自谦在众多人才中略有成就，后也比喻出类拔萃的人才。

examples.zh: 他在同龄人中桂林一枝，年纪轻轻就拿了大奖。
examples.en: Among his peers he stands out; he won a major prize at a young age.

examples.zh: 这位新科状元，真可谓桂林一枝。
examples.en: This new top scorer is truly one of a kind.

story.en: Xi Shen, asked by Emperor Wu of Jin how he rated himself after topping the examination, said he was like one branch of the cassia grove, a piece of jade from Mount Kun.
story.zh: 《晋书·郤诜传》：“臣举贤良对策为天下第一，犹桂林之一枝，昆山之片玉。”

usage.en: Often paired with 昆山片玉. Literary, praise; originally modest self-description.
usage.zh: 常与“昆山片玉”并用，书面语，含赞美，原为自谦。

pinyin: xué hǎo bù yì, xué huài róng yì
literal: learn · good · not · easy, learn · bad · easy
natural: learning good is hard, learning bad is easy

meaning.en: Good habits take effort to acquire, but bad habits are picked up effortlessly.
meaning.zh: 养成好习惯很难，染上坏习惯却很容易。

equivalents: bad habits are easy to pick up
it's easier to go downhill than up

examples.zh: 学好不易，学坏容易，家长要多留意孩子交什么朋友。
examples.en: Good habits are hard to learn and bad ones easy; parents should watch who their children befriend.

examples.zh: 学好不易，学坏容易，他跟着混了几个月就开始抽烟了。
examples.en: It's hard to improve and easy to go astray; after a few months in that crowd he started smoking.

usage.en: A warning in parenting and education. Casual.
usage.zh: 多用于家教、教育中的告诫，口语。

meaning.en: To attack a point the enemy must defend, forcing them to give up their own plans.
meaning.zh: 攻击对方必定要救援的地方，迫使对方改变计划。

examples.zh: 球队攻其必救，逼得对手回防，赢得了空档。
examples.en: The team attacked where the opponent had to defend, drawing them back and opening space.

examples.zh: 谈判时他攻其必救，对方只好让步。
examples.en: In the negotiation he pressed on the point they had to protect, and they gave in.

usage.en: Strategy term; extends to sports and business. The classic example is 围魏救赵.
usage.zh: 兵法用语，也用于体育、商战，典型战例是“围魏救赵”。

literal: take up · brush · at once · complete
natural: pick up the brush and finish at once

meaning.en: To write an essay or poem quickly and fluently, with almost no preparation.
meaning.zh: 拿起笔来立刻写成，形容文思敏捷，写得又快又好。

examples.zh: 他才思敏捷，援笔立成，一篇评论半小时就写好了。
examples.en: With his quick mind he dashed off a commentary in half an hour.

examples.zh: 宴席上众人请他赋诗，他援笔立成。
examples.en: At the banquet everyone asked for a poem, and he wrote it on the spot.

natural: loosen the clothes and undo the belt

meaning.en: To take off one's outer clothes and loosen the belt, as for bed or to relax.
meaning.zh: 脱下外衣，解开腰带，准备休息或放松。

examples.zh: 他回到家，宽衣解带，倒在床上就睡着了。
examples.en: He got home, took off his clothes, fell on the bed and was asleep.

examples.zh: 大夫让病人宽衣解带，仔细检查腹部。
examples.en: The doctor asked the patient to loosen their clothes for an abdominal check.

usage.en: A narrative phrase, used for undressing before bed or an examination; in literary writing it can hint at intimacy.
usage.zh: 叙述性词语，用于睡前更衣或检查身体，文学语境中有时暗示亲密。

natural: stop walking and not go forward

meaning.en: To stop advancing; to stay put out of fear, laziness or complacency.
meaning.zh: 停下脚步，不再向前，指因畏难、懒惰或自满而不再进步。

examples.zh: 遇到一点挫折就止步不前，是不会成功的。
examples.en: Stopping at the first setback will not lead to success.

examples.zh: 公司若满足于现状而止步不前，就会被市场淘汰。
examples.en: If a company is content with the status quo and stands still, the market will weed it out.

usage.en: Usually as a criticism or warning. Predicate.
usage.zh: 多用于批评或告诫，作谓语。

meaning.en: When a woman's looks fade, the favour she enjoyed declines; a warning about relationships built on appearance.
meaning.zh: 容貌衰老，受到的宠爱也随之减退。

examples.zh: 深宫里的嫔妃，往往色衰爱弛，晚景凄凉。
examples.en: Concubines in the inner palace often lost favour as their beauty faded and ended their days in loneliness.

examples.zh: 她明白色衰爱弛的道理，所以拼命工作，不依赖任何人。
examples.en: She understands that love fades with beauty, so she works hard and relies on nobody.

story.en: Shiji records the saying that those who serve others with their looks see love decline once their looks fade (以色事人者，色衰而爱弛).
story.zh: 《史记·吕不韦列传》：“以色事人者，色衰而爱弛。”

usage.en: Used in historical or critical contexts about relationships based on looks or favour. Literary.
usage.zh: 多用于历史或批评以色相、恩宠维系的关系，书面语。

literal: the more · trace · the more · black
natural: the more you trace over it, the blacker it gets

meaning.en: The more you try to explain or fix a mistake, the worse it looks.
meaning.zh: 越是解释、掩饰，反而越让人觉得有问题。

equivalents: dig oneself deeper into a hole

examples.zh: 你别再解释了，越描越黑。
examples.en: Stop explaining, you're only making it look worse.

examples.zh: 公司的澄清声明越描越黑，反而引来更多质疑。
examples.en: The company's clarification only made things worse and drew more doubts.

usage.en: A warning not to over-explain; casual. Related to 欲盖弥彰.
usage.zh: 劝人不要过度解释，口语，与“欲盖弥彰”相近。

meaning.en: If a relationship has to end, part on good terms.
meaning.zh: 既然相聚过，分开时也应和平体面，不要闹僵。

examples.zh: 我们好聚好散，分手后还是朋友。
examples.en: Let's part on good terms and stay friends after the breakup.

examples.zh: 合伙生意做不下去了，大家好聚好散吧。
examples.en: The partnership isn't working; let's end it amicably.

usage.en: Said about breakups, divorce or ending a business; often with 要. Casual.
usage.zh: 多用于分手、离婚、散伙，常说“要好聚好散”，口语。

pinyin: yīng xióng bù wèn chū chù
natural: heroes aren't asked where they came from

meaning.en: A person's worth lies in ability and achievements, not in family background.
meaning.zh: 评价人才看本事和成就，而不看出身。

equivalents: it doesn't matter where you come from
judge a man by his deeds

examples.zh: 英雄不问出处，只要有能力，我们就重用。
examples.en: We don't ask where a hero comes from; if you have the ability, we'll promote you.

examples.zh: 他出身贫寒却成了科学家，真是英雄不问出处。
examples.en: Born poor, he became a scientist; heroes are not judged by origins.

usage.en: Often used to encourage the humble-born. Neutral, positive tone.
usage.zh: 常用来鼓励出身寒微的人，语气积极。

pinyin: rěn yī shí fēng píng làng jìng
variants: 忍一时风平浪静，退一步海阔天空
literal: endure · one · moment · wind · calm · waves · still
natural: bear it for a moment and the storm calms

meaning.en: Holding your temper for a moment spares you a big quarrel.
meaning.zh: 暂时忍让一下，就能避免冲突，事情平安过去。

examples.zh: 忍一时风平浪静，他咽下了这口气，没有和邻居吵架。
examples.en: Bear it a moment and the storm passes; he swallowed his anger and didn't quarrel with the neighbour.

examples.zh: 婆媳之间，忍一时风平浪静，退一步海阔天空。
examples.en: Between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, a little patience smooths things over, and stepping back opens the sky.

usage.en: Usually completed with 退一步海阔天空. Advice for avoiding conflict; casual.
usage.zh: 常与“退一步海阔天空”连用，劝人避免冲突，口语。

natural: ten years to hone one sword

meaning.en: To spend many years perfecting one skill or project before showing it to the world.
meaning.zh: 用很长的时间磨炼一项本领或打磨一件作品。

equivalents: years of preparation for one big moment

examples.zh: 十年磨一剑，这部纪录片他拍了整整十年。
examples.en: It took ten years to hone this one blade; he spent a full decade filming this documentary.

examples.zh: 经过十年磨一剑的苦练，她终于夺得了冠军。
examples.en: After ten years of honing her craft, she finally won the championship.

story.en: Jia Dao's poem 'The Swordsman' reads 'Ten years I have ground one sword; its frosty edge has never been tried.'
story.zh: 贾岛《剑客》：“十年磨一剑，霜刃未曾试。”

usage.en: Often followed by 霜刃未曾试 in the original line. Today praises long preparation.
usage.zh: 原诗下句是“霜刃未曾试”。今多夸赞长期积累、精益求精。

synonyms: 台上一分钟，台下十年功

meaning.en: A fine child can come from a poor family or a bad parent.
meaning.zh: 不好的父母或环境里，也能出现优秀的孩子。

equivalents: a good egg from a bad nest

examples.zh: 他爸爸是个赌徒，他却勤奋上进，真是歹竹出好笋。
examples.en: His father is a gambler but he is hardworking; a good shoot from bad bamboo.

examples.zh: 大家都夸这孩子懂事，歹竹出好笋啊。
examples.en: Everyone praises how sensible the child is; fine fruit from a poor tree.

usage.en: Often said with surprise; the 'bad' refers to parents or background, not the child. Casual, can sound rude about the parents.
usage.zh: 常带惊讶口吻，“歹”指父母或环境，口语，对父母有些不敬。

antonyms: 龙生龙，凤生凤，老鼠的儿子会打洞

pinyin: guò rì zi cái zhī yóu yán guì
literal: live · days · only then · know · oil · salt · dear
natural: only when you run a household do you know how dear oil and salt are

meaning.en: You only appreciate how hard it is to make ends meet once you run a household yourself.
meaning.zh: 自己当家过日子，才知道生活开支的不易。

equivalents: you don't know the cost of living until you pay the bills

examples.zh: 刚结婚才发现，过日子才知油盐贵。
examples.en: Newly married, I find you only learn the price of oil and salt when you keep house.

examples.zh: 妈妈说，过日子才知油盐贵，让我别乱花钱。
examples.en: Mum said you only know what things cost when you run a home, and told me not to waste money.

usage.en: Said to young people who spend freely. Casual, domestic tone.
usage.zh: 多用来劝花钱大手大脚的年轻人，口语，家常。

meaning.en: Of a woman: to leave one man and marry another; by extension, to switch allegiance.
meaning.zh: 旧指女子改嫁；也比喻另投靠他人。

examples.zh: 戏里的她丈夫去世后，没有琵琶别抱，独自抚养孩子。
examples.en: In the play, she did not remarry after her husband died and raised the child alone.

examples.zh: 他在公司落难时琵琶别抱，投奔了对手。
examples.en: He switched sides when the firm ran into trouble, running to the rival.

usage.en: Dated and literary; the image comes from a woman holding a pipa. Can sound disparaging of women; use with care.
usage.zh: 陈旧的书面语，来自女子抱琵琶的形象，对女性有贬抑色彩，使用需谨慎。

meaning.en: Children say whatever they think, so what they say should not be taken as offence or ill omen.
meaning.zh: 小孩子说话天真直率，不必忌讳，也不必当真。

equivalents: out of the mouths of babes

examples.zh: 别生气，童言无忌，他不是故意的。
examples.en: Don't be angry; kids say what they think and he didn't mean it.

examples.zh: 小侄女说我胖，大家哈哈大笑，童言无忌嘛。
examples.en: My little niece said I was fat and everyone laughed; children speak without guile.

usage.en: Said to smooth over a child's blunt remark. Warm, neutral tone.
usage.zh: 用来化解孩子说话直率造成的尴尬，语气温和。

meaning.en: To lack the most basic common sense about everyday things, or to have no practical experience.
meaning.zh: 连豆子和麦子都分不清，形容缺乏生活常识，或不懂实际事务。

equivalents: not know a thing about farming

examples.zh: 这些城里长大的孩子，不辨菽麦，见了麦田都不认识。
examples.en: Raised in the city, these children can't tell beans from wheat and don't recognise a wheat field.

examples.zh: 书呆子往往不辨菽麦，缺乏实际经验。
examples.en: Bookworms often lack practical sense and experience.

story.en: The Zuozhuan says the elder brother of Lord Dao of Jin was 'without wit and could not tell beans from wheat', so he was not made ruler.
story.zh: 《左传·成公十八年》：“周子有兄而无慧，不能辨菽麦，故不可立。”

usage.en: Often paired with 四体不勤. Literary or teasing.
usage.zh: 常与“四体不勤”连用，书面或调侃。

meaning.en: Farming is hard work; one should know how hard it is to produce food.
meaning.zh: 种庄稼、收粮食非常辛苦，提醒人们要体会劳动的艰辛。

equivalents: know the hard work behind every meal

examples.zh: 老师要孩子们去农村体验，让他们懂得稼穑艰难。
examples.en: The teacher took the children to the countryside so they would understand the toil of farming.

examples.zh: 不知稼穑艰难，就不会珍惜每一粒粮食。
examples.en: Without knowing how hard farming is, you won't cherish every grain.

story.en: The Book of Documents (Wu Yi) says that a ruler who first knows the hardship of farming will be at ease in governing.
story.zh: 《尚书·无逸》：“君子所其无逸。先知稼穑之艰难乃逸。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前11—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 11th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Used to teach thrift and respect for labour. 稼 jià, 穑 sè. Literary.
usage.zh: 用来教人节俭、尊重劳动。“稼”读jià，“穑”读sè，书面语。

synonyms: 谁知盘中餐，粒粒皆辛苦

natural: hold a regret all one's life

meaning.en: To carry a regret for life over something one failed to do or achieve.
meaning.zh: 因为某件事没做成或没做好，一辈子感到遗憾。

examples.zh: 没能见到母亲最后一面，他抱憾终身。
examples.en: He never got to see his mother one last time and regretted it for life.

examples.zh: 那一球要是进了就夺冠，他至今仍抱憾终身。
examples.en: If that shot had gone in they would have won; he still regrets it all his life.

usage.en: Often 令他抱憾终身. Predicate.
usage.zh: 常说“令他抱憾终身”，作谓语。
